en: The Ritual Manual for the Cultivation of the Five-Syllable Mantra of Vairocana,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra by Imperial Order. Now,
in cultivating and accomplishing the Buddha-dharma of Vairocana, one should first go to a secluded and pure place.

One should smear the ground with cow dung, sprinkle it with scented water, burn various kinds of famous incense, and scatter various seasonal flowers; then, in a state of tranquility, one should perform the rites amidst the bustle, bathe until pure, put on fresh clean garments, and sit in the full lotus posture.
Alternatively, one may sit according to the specific category of rite:
for pacifying and auspicious rites, sit in the *śāntika-śrī-sana* facing north;
for increasing rites, sit in the *puṣṭi-padma-sana* facing east.
For the rite of attraction (*vaśīkaraṇa*), one sits in the vajra-posture facing west;
for the rite of subjugation (*abhicāruka*), one sits in a squatting posture with the feet pressing against each other facing south.
One may sit according to whichever direction one prefers. Then, having smeared one's hands with fragrant clay, one joins the palms at the crown of the head and pays homage to all the Buddhas.

Then, from below, one should visualize the syllable *vaḥ* arising from the wind-circle (*vāyu-maṇḍala*), adorned with two dots (*bindu*), shaped like gold and emitting blazing light, fierce and resplendent.

The vajra-flames shatter the great earth and surge upward; one should then imagine these vajra-flames incinerating one’s own body until it is reduced to ashes, which follow the four types of dharmic colors.
One should imagine the ashes forming a maṇḍala, and within that maṇḍala, visualize a single lotus flower.
Within the lotus, visualize that the syllable *vāṃ* transforms into the form of a vajra;
visualize your own body as being composed of vajras.
Then, perform the samaya-mudrā:
Form the *tripuṭa* hand gesture with both hands, extend the two thumbs, and empower the five places [of the body].
The mantra is: *Namo samantabuddhānām asame trisame samaye svāhā*. Next, form the Dharma-realm mudrā (*dharmadhātu-mudrā*).
Form two fists with both hands, placing the two thumbs inside the palms and extending the two index fingers;
visualize the syllable *raṃ* above the crown of the head, contemplate the meaning of reality, and realize that all dharmas and sense objects are unattainable.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ dharmadhātu svabhāvātmaka hūṃ. Next, perform the seal of the wheel:
interlace the two hands with palms facing outward, and place the two thumbs against each other within the right palm.
Visualize yourself as Vajrasattva and empower [yourself] by joining [the hands].
The mantra is: "Namo samanta-vajrāṇāṃ vajra-tama kuṃhaṃ. Next, perform the armor mudrā:

With both hands in the *tripuṭa* (three-fold) gesture, bend the two index fingers so they rest against the upper joints of the middle fingers; the two thumbs are held upright and joined together at the five points of the palms.

The mantra is: *Namaḥ samanta-vajrāṇāṃ vajrakavaca hūṃ*. Then, one should visualize a great lotus king before oneself; within that lotus, one visualizes a golden syllable *kha*. That syllable *kha* transforms into the Bhagavat, the Great Heroic Honored One, who abides in *samādhi* and forms the sword mudrā (*khaḍgamudrā*).
Then, forming the Tathāgata Hook Seal (Tathāgatāṅkuśamudrā) to invite the Honored One:
interlace the two hands inwardly to form fists, extend the right index finger like a hook, and beckon it toward oneself.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namo samantabuddhānām | Aḥ sarvātman-pratihatat-tadgocure jñātidhāriye paripūrake svāhā. Once the noble assembly has arrived, one should immediately offer argha water; holding it with both hands at the forehead, one should visualize bathing the noble assembly.
The mantra is: "Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ oṃ na samasama svāhā. Next, perform the mudrā for offering the seat:
join the two hands with palms hollowed together, then extend and slightly bend the six fingers so they resemble the shape of a lotus flower.
The mantra is: *Namo samantabuddhānām aḥ*. Next, form the mudrā of the Noble Acala: with both hands, make fists; extend the index and middle fingers of each hand;

press the ring and little fingers with the two thumbs. Let the left hand serve as the sheath and the right hand as the blade. Rotate the blade counter-clockwise to dispel all demonic obstacles, and rotate it clockwise and up and down to establish the boundaries of the directions and intermediate points.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samanta-vajrāya caṇḍa-mahā-roṣaṇa-sphoṭaya hūṃ trāṭ hūṃ khaṃ. Furthermore, one should touch the incense and flowers with the sword mudrā, seeking stainlessness to purify them; having thus performed the consecration, they are placed within the scabbard.
Next, form the five-syllable sword mudrā of Vairocana:
join the two hands in *añjali*, bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch, forming the shape of a sword.
The mantra is as follows:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Avira hūṃ khaṃ. Next, form the incense-offering mudrā (*gandhamudrā*):
turn the palm of the right hand outward, and grasp the right wrist with the left hand as if forming a ring.
The mantra is: *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vidyājvālana-bhe svāhā*. Next, form the Flower Mudrā:
interlace the two hands with palms facing upward, extend the index fingers, and place the two thumbs beneath the lower joints of the index fingers.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ mahāmaitry-abhyudgate svāhā*. Next, form the incense mudrā: join the backs of the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands and extend them upward;
extend the index fingers straight and incline them so they touch each other; place the thumbs beneath the joints of the index fingers.
The mantra is: *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ dharmadhātuvana-gate svāhā*. Next, form the mudrā for food and drink:
join the palms of the concentration and wisdom hands, with the five fingers interlaced; this is the universal offering mudrā for holding various substances.
*Namo samantabuddhānām arara karara malinadana me svāhā.* Next, perform the lamp mudrā:

form a fist with the right hand, extend the middle finger straight upward, bend the index finger to press against the base of the thumb, and place the tip of the index finger against the middle finger.

The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ dharmatā-dhiti-sarvārthavabhāsana-ogha-udaye svāhā*. The offered unguents, flower garlands, incense, food and drink, and lamps are presented as offerings according to the four types of ritual colors. By means of the five mudrās of offering, one accomplishes a universal ocean-like cloud of incense, flowers, and other offerings for the assembly of the noble ones.
Next, form the Seal of Perfection:
Join the two hands with palms hollowed together and place them upon the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām aḥ vi-
Sama-ye-spa-ra-he-maṃ.
Oṃ oṃ na jñāna-dharmatā-vākṣa.
Samayā svadhātathāgataḥ
Pariccha-maṇḍala-māma-bhūja-melana.
tathāgatādhiṣṭhānamantracaryeṇa me (or mayi) /

*Svāhā*. By means of this mantra and mudrā, one performs offerings of clouds and oceans of incense, flowers, and so forth; if these are not actually present, one instead applies the five syllables from the lower part of the body up to the crown of the head—representing earth, water, fire, wind, and space—and visualizes oneself as the golden Vairocana Buddha, with a radiant halo, a crown, necklaces, and clad in fine silken garments.
Then, forming the sword mudrā:

place it at the heart while abiding in samādhi; holding the rosary with both hands joined within the palms, recite the mantra seven times, and having empowered it, place it upon the crown of the head.
The mantra is: "Oṃ vairocana-mara svāhā. Then, placing both hands at the heart, hold the rosary and recite the mantra of the deity for the prescribed number of times.
Having finished, place the jewel in the palms of the hands and, with palms joined at the crown of the head, dedicate the merit and make this aspiration:
"By this merit, may all sentient beings swiftly realize the state of Vairocana Buddha!"

Having released the rosary, one then forms the seal of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*) and sits upright with the body straightened. One visualizes the white syllable *Aṃ* at the crown of the head;

upon the pupils of the two eyes, one visualizes the syllable *Laṃ*. Then, slightly bowing the head, one focuses the mind on the space between the breasts and visualizes a full moon disc. Upon this moon disc, one arranges five syllables:
one visualizes the syllable *A* in the center as golden in color, while the remaining four syllables are placed arranged clockwise.
The true meaning of the five syllables is as follows:
the syllable "A" signifies that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen;
the syllable "Vi" signifies that the conceptualization of all phenomena is inexpressible.
The syllable *ra* signifies that all phenomena are free from dust;
the syllable *ha* signifies that the cause of all phenomena is unapprehendable;
the syllable *kha* signifies that all things are like space and are unapprehendable.
This is called mental recitation.
Then, forming the sword mudrā, recite [the mantra] seven times and scatter it over the crown of the head;
next, form the five-fold offering mudrā, present the argha water, and offer praise.
Form the Immovable Sword Mudrā and rotate it counter-clockwise to dissolve the boundary;
form the Samaya Mudrā and place it upon the crown of the head, reciting [the mantra] three times while visualizing the sending off of the noble assembly.

Prostrate to the Buddha and rise; perform walking meditation as desired and read or recite Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras. Dedicate this merit to all sentient beings, wishing that their heart's desires may be swiftly fulfilled and that they achieve both mundane and supramundane *siddhi*.

*Vairocana-nenju*, one fascicle. In the summer of the first year of the Enkyō era, this manual was carved using the legacy left by my deceased younger brother, the monk Sōsonryū, in order to fulfill his long-held aspiration. I humbly pray that the milk of the Dharma may eternally moisten the entire Dharmadhātu. Recorded respectfully by Fujiwara Tsunaka.
In the eighth month of autumn, the first year of the Enkyō era (the Jiazi year), I reflected upon the incomparable collation of Mount Sambong.
